sections.text: In 2011, Somali gunmen killed David Tebbutt and abducted his wife Judith in Kenya. Kenyan police arrested Ali Kololo, a woodcutter, and tortured him into signing a statement. Metropolitan Police officers assisted the investigation. Former Detective Superintendent Neil Hibberd presented misleading evidence and relied on Kololo's coerced statement, leading to Kololo's wrongful conviction for kidnap and robbery.

The wrongful imprisonment destroyed Kololo's health, marriage and family life, leaving him unable to work or support his children.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: UK net migration fell to 77,000 in the year to June, down from 204,000 in the previous 12 months and a peak of 944,000 in 2023. This marks the lowest level since 1997 excluding the Covid pandemic. The decline was driven by drops in work visas, student arrivals, and asylum claims, following visa restrictions introduced by successive Conservative and Labour administrations.

sections.heading: Why it matters
